drug_class: CFTR Modulator Combination (Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator Modulators)
purpose: This medicine is used to treat cystic fibrosis (CF) in patients who have at least one copy of a specific gene mutation called F508del, or certain other mutations approved for this drug. It helps improve lung function and quality of life for people living with CF. Your doctor will confirm if your specific gene type makes you a good candidate for this medication.
how_it_works: In cystic fibrosis, a faulty protein causes thick, sticky mucus to build up in the lungs and other organs. Think of this protein like a broken door that won't open properly. Elexacaftor and tezacaftor work together to help the protein get to the right place and fold correctly, while ivacaftor acts like a key that helps keep that door open so the protein can work the way it should.
common_side_effects: Upper respiratory infections like the common cold, headache, stomach pain, diarrhea, rash, increased liver enzymes (your doctor will monitor this with blood tests), dizziness, and runny nose are among the most commonly reported side effects.
warnings: This medication can affect your liver, so your doctor will check your liver with blood tests before you start and regularly while you take it. Tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain. It can also cause eye problems in some younger patients, so eye exams may be recommended. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the drug level in your body. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as many drugs can interact with Trikafta.
typical_dosing: For adults and children 6 years and older, the usual dose is three tablets in the morning (two fixed-dose tablets of elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor) and one tablet of ivacaftor alone in the evening, about 12 hours apart. Always take this medicine with a fat-containing food, like eggs, butter, peanut butter, or cheese, to help your body absorb it properly. Dosing for younger children may differ, so always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
